description: Open-source unified metadata platform for data discovery, data observability, and data governance powered by a central metadata repository

key_requirements: State changes made to the code
license.recommendation: Excellent for commercial and open-source reuse. Very permissive with minimal restrictions. Safe for derivative works and commercial applications.

architecture.overview: Four-layer architecture with JSON Schema-based metadata model

core_components.name: Metadata Store
core_components.description: Central repository managing the metadata graph

core_components.name: Metadata APIs
core_components.description: RESTful interfaces for metadata production and consumption

core_components.name: Ingestion Framework
core_components.description: Pluggable system for metadata extraction from diverse sources

metadata_model.approach: JSON Schema-based with strong typing and extensibility

schema_organization.entity: Core metadata objects (tables, dashboards, pipelines, etc.)

key_entities.name: Table
key_features: Table types: Regular, View, MaterializedView, Iceberg, Stream
Column-level metadata with data types, constraints, ordinal positions

key_entities.name: GlossaryTerm
features: Mutually exclusive rules for child terms

custom_properties.uniqueness: Property name must be unique per entity
property_types: Dates and times with format specifications
features: Display names separate from internal names
Type safety through property type references

extensibility.extension_object: Generic extension object for additional properties on core entities

design_patterns: JSON Schema for type safety and validation
Entity references via UUID and FQN (Fully Qualified Name)

components.nodes: All entities in the lineage graph excluding primary entity

parameterization.required_optional: Parameters can be marked required or optional

execution_features: Parameter name-value pairs with runtime conversion

connector_framework.architecture: Pluggable Python-based system with Airflow integration

source.description: Data origin with connector type and service connection

control_settings.raiseOnError: Flag workflow as failed on processing errors

design_patterns: Shared base classes for similar connectors

followers.description: Users can follow data assets, glossaries, and other entities

design_patterns: Unified thread model for all collaboration types
Vector search support for semantic discovery

domains.purpose: Bounded contexts aligned with business units or functions

policies.rules: Multiple access control rules per policy
policies.scoping: Applied to teams, roles, and domains

data_products.purpose: Group related data assets as products

categories.name: Raw Cost Analysis
categories.description: Unprocessed cost data for financial tracking

analytics_and_insights.time_series: All metrics are timestamped for trend analysis

metadata_management.description: All entities defined via JSON Schema for strong typing and validation
Metadata stored as a graph with typed relationships
All entities identified by UUID with FQN as alternative
All entities versioned with change tracking
Entities marked as deleted rather than removed

api_design.description: Standard CRUD operations plus advanced search
Paginated responses for large result sets

data_quality.description: Reusable test definitions instantiated as test cases
Support for Great Expectations, dbt, Soda, etc.
Group tests by dimensions for granular analysis

collaboration.description: Single schema for conversations, tasks, and announcements
Users can follow entities for updates

factors: Complex domain model with 100+ entity types

deployment_complexity.quickstart: Docker Compose makes initial setup easy

for_reuse.rationale: Well-designed, extensible, and comprehensive. Can be adopted wholesale or adapted.
Graph-based with rich edge metadata. Column-level support. Multiple source types.
Flexible, multi-platform, well-structured with test definitions and cases.
Excellent patterns but 84+ connectors may be too many. Adopt the architecture and select specific connectors.
Unified thread model is elegant. Implementation may be overkill for some use cases.
Hierarchical domains with ownership and access control. Well-designed.
Modern React stack with excellent visualizations. May want to adapt rather than adopt directly.
RESTful with OpenAPI, consistent patterns, well-documented.

for_uml_codex.recommendation: Adopt JSON Schema approach for UML model representation
for_uml_codex.rationale: Provides type safety, validation, and documentation. Can generate code from schemas.

for_uml_codex.recommendation: Study lineage graph model for relationship tracking
for_uml_codex.rationale: UML diagrams are graphs. OpenMetadata's approach to graph representation is relevant.
Multi-tenancy and organization will be important for enterprise UML modeling.

for_uml_codex.recommendation: Learn from data quality patterns for UML model validation
for_uml_codex.rationale: UML models need validation. Test definition + test case pattern is applicable.

for_uml_codex.recommendation: Study collaboration patterns for team-based modeling
for_uml_codex.rationale: UML modeling is often collaborative. Thread model and tasks are relevant.

for_uml_codex.recommendation: Consider connector framework pattern for model importers/exporters
for_uml_codex.rationale: UML Codex will need to import/export from various tools. Connector pattern is proven.

for_uml_codex.recommendation: Adopt custom properties pattern for UML stereotype extensions
for_uml_codex.rationale: UML stereotypes and tagged values are similar to custom properties.

for_uml_codex.recommendation: Study versioning and change tracking patterns
for_uml_codex.rationale: UML models evolve. Version control is essential.

cautions.caution: Full adoption would be very complex. Be selective.
cautions.mitigation: Start with core patterns (schemas, lineage, domains) and expand.

cautions.caution: Three-language stack (Java, TypeScript, Python) increases maintenance burden.
cautions.mitigation: Consider if all three are necessary for your use case.

cautions.caution: Many dependencies to manage and update.
cautions.mitigation: Carefully evaluate each dependency. Consider lighter alternatives.
Evaluate if full-text search is needed or if simpler solutions suffice.
Evaluate if workflow automation is needed for initial version.

documentation.quality: Comprehensive with quickstart, deployment, connectors, API docs

key_takeaways.takeaway: OpenMetadata is a comprehensive, production-grade metadata management platform
key_takeaways.implication: Full adoption would be a major undertaking. Selective pattern reuse is recommended.

key_takeaways.takeaway: JSON Schema-based metadata model is excellent
key_takeaways.implication: This pattern is highly reusable and should be considered for UML Codex.

key_takeaways.takeaway: Graph-based lineage tracking is sophisticated and proven
key_takeaways.implication: Relevant for UML relationship tracking. Study and adapt.
Connector architecture is solid. Adopt patterns, not necessarily all connectors.
Important for enterprise UML modeling. Consider early adoption.

key_takeaways.takeaway: Data quality framework is flexible and multi-platform
key_takeaways.implication: Test definition + test case pattern applicable to UML validation.
May be overkill initially, but patterns are valuable for future.

key_takeaways.takeaway: Modern React UI with excellent visualizations
key_takeaways.implication: Good reference for UML diagram visualization. ReactFlow is particularly relevant.
Code and patterns can be freely reused in commercial or open-source projects.
Patterns are battle-tested and continuously improved.
